production.note: Calendar years. Start: Evo (Jethro Bovingdon, 2 Dec 2022): "The Zonda F was launched in 2005, at Geneva once again"; the car tested was "1 of 25" coupes. End year PROVISIONAL: Supercar Nostalgia (supercarnostalgia-zonda-f, an enthusiast site): "Zonda F production ended in 2011 following the completion of 25 Coupes and 25 Roadsters." That end year covers the Roadster F as well; when the last coupe was built was not found. The Roadster F is a separate model; the Clubsport (650 CV) is a higher-output version.

body.note: Coupe; the Zonda Roadster F is sold under its own name.

configuration.note: "Mercedes-Benz AMG 12 cylinder V 60°; 48 valves; displacement 7291 cc"

aspiration.note: No forced induction listed for the AMG V12.

transmission.note: "Mechanical 6 speed (+ reverse)"; Evo: "The only transmission available was a Cima six-speed manual."

powerHp.note: Pagani's rating is metric: 443 kW x 1.34102 = 594 hp (602 CV x 0.98632 = 594 hp). Quote (pagani.com, kW (hp)/rpm column): "(443) 602/6150". Evo's spec panel (evo-zonda-f): "Power | 594bhp @ 6150rpm". The Clubsport version is listed at "(478) 650/6200" and is not this record.

weightLb.note: DRY weight (step 4), for a car with carbon-ceramic brakes and without the Comfort Pack: 1,230 kg x 2.20462 = 2,712 lb. Quote (pagani.com): "1230 kg (without Comfort Pack and with CCM brakes)". Evo's spec panel: "Weight (dry) | 1230kg". No curb weight was found (steps 1 to 3). Pagani's qualification suggests the CCM brakes were an option, so the figure is labelled lightweight-options; a standard car would be somewhat heavier.

sources.title: Pagani Zonda F review - revisiting an analogue icon

provisionalNote: Production end year (2011) is provisional: it rests on an enthusiast site (Supercar Nostalgia) and covers the Zonda F coupe and Roadster F together. A Pagani or major-magazine statement of when the last Zonda F coupe was built would replace it. Power (594 hp) and dry weight (2,712 lb) are from Pagani, confirmed by Evo's spec panel.
